page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-48 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity totals 384.0 GB of RAM, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong uncached memory throughput, achieving 212.65 GB/sec on large block read operations and 98.19 GB/sec on large block write operations, both ranking in the top 25%. Network and I/O handling is also efficient, with static web serving throughput reaching 47.78 GB/sec. General compute metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 38,234.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,383.0, place the machine in the middle 50% tier.

Cost efficiency is centered around large-scale in-memory footprint consolidation. Because storage must be provisioned externally via network-attached volumes, overall infrastructure spend is best justified by tasks that actively utilize the 384 GB memory pool rather than raw floating-point speed. The platform fits memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, extensive database operations, software compilation jobs, and data caching tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-48 is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz and 384.0 GB of RAM. The instance includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 and AES instructions, but does not provide local storage or discrete GPUs. In benchmark testing, the n2-highmem-48 demonstrates top-quartile large-block uncached memory throughput, achieving 212.65 GB/sec for reads and 98.19 GB/sec for writes, alongside strong static web serving throughput of 47.78 GB/sec. Compute and synthetic processor benchmarks, including Geekbench and PassMark, reflect middle-tier performance consistent with high-density general execution. With 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy operations, making it well-suited for large in-memory caches, enterprise database deployments, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
